description.summary: Smile Dog (also written Smile.jpg) is an image-based creepypasta about an allegedly cursed photograph of a husky-like dog with human-style teeth. The accompanying short story is most often attributed to Michael Lutz, who posted a canonical version to the Creepypasta Wiki in August 2010.
description.full: Smile Dog is one of the foundational creepypasta legends of the late-2000s anglophone internet. The story centers on a digital image — known as Smile.jpg — that allegedly causes anyone who views it to suffer nightmares, sleep paralysis, and mental breakdown until they 'spread the word' by passing the image on to others. The framing story is told from the perspective of a writer, 'Mr. L', who interviews victims of the image. The image and its associated lore appear to have first surfaced on 4chan's /x/ (paranormal) board around 2008. The most-cited canonical text was uploaded to the Creepypasta Wiki on August 27, 2010 by Michael Lutz; this version of the story has been the basis for most subsequent retellings. Like Slender Man and other early creepypasta, Smile Dog is studied as a case of digital folklore (Trevor J. Blank, Lynne S. McNeill) and is broadly understood as fiction; no version of the image has ever been independently verified to cause harm.

etymology.origin: Internet — emerged on imageboards (4chan /x/) circa 2008, codified on Creepypasta Wiki in 2010.
etymology.meaning: Refers to the unsettling smile (with apparent human teeth) of the dog in the image.
etymology.first_use: First image circulation on 4chan, c. 2008; first canonical text on Creepypasta Wiki, August 27, 2010.

features.description: The image depicts a dog resembling a husky
An open-mouth grin showing what appear to be human-like teeth — the visual hook of the image
Most circulating versions of the image include a partially visible human hand

physical.morphology: A static fictional image; no behaviour outside narrative attribution.

abilities.description: In the fiction, viewing the image is said to cause nightmares, sleep paralysis, and ultimately mental breakdown unless the viewer 'spreads the word' by sharing it with others
Smile Dog is said to appear in victims' dreams demanding they 'spread the word'

patterns: Spreads from victim to victim through the act of sharing the image
Frames itself as a chain-letter / contagion narrative

range.description: An internet-native fiction: distribution is anywhere the anglophone internet reaches. The originating community is North American imageboard culture (4chan) and the wider Creepypasta Wiki community.

hotspots.name: 4chan /x/ (origin)
hotspots.notes: Apparent first circulation site of the Smile.jpg image and associated story.

hotspots.notes: Canonical version of the Smile Dog story uploaded by Michael Lutz on 27 August 2010.

first_recorded.source: Reported initial circulation on 4chan /x/ (per Know Your Meme and Wikipedia)

peak_activity_periods.description: Canonical Lutz text on Creepypasta Wiki

origins.cultural_roots: Late-2000s imageboard culture, particularly 4chan's /x/ (paranormal) board, and the early Creepypasta Wiki community.
origins.earliest_accounts: Story circulation on 4chan /x/ around 2008; canonical text by Michael Lutz on Creepypasta Wiki, August 27, 2010.
origins.folklore_connections: Part of the early-2010s wave of creepypasta that includes Slender Man, The Rake, and Jeff the Killer.

timeline.event: Smile.jpg image and associated story begin circulating on 4chan's /x/ board
Earliest documented Urban Dictionary entry for 'Smile.jpg' is created
timeline.source: Know Your Meme entry, citing Urban Dictionary

timeline.event: Michael Lutz uploads the canonical 'Smile Dog' creepypasta to the Creepypasta Wiki

history.modern_era: Smile Dog remains a recognised reference point in creepypasta history, regularly cited alongside Slender Man and The Rake in writings on early digital folklore. The image continues to be retold on YouTube, TikTok, and Reddit, and has inspired fan art and a number of unofficial games and animations.

photographic.name: Smile.jpg
photographic.description: Original Smile.jpg image of a husky-like dog with apparent human teeth; circulated widely online from 2008.
photographic.analysis: Authorship of the image itself is unknown. Treated as fiction; no claim of supernatural effect has been substantiated.

documentary.name: Michael Lutz, 'Smile Dog' (2010)
documentary.description: Canonical Creepypasta Wiki version of the Smile Dog story.
documentary.analysis: Acknowledged fiction; widely treated as the definitive textual version of the legend.

scientific.name: Digital folklore
scientific.description: Folklorists treat Smile Dog as an early example of internet-native folklore: anonymously authored, collectively elaborated, image-driven, and self-replicating in the manner of a chain letter.
evidence_cited: Pattern of imageboard origin and wiki canonisation
Self-replicating 'spread the word' mechanic embedded in the fiction

skeptical.name: Acknowledged fiction
skeptical.description: Smile Dog is an explicitly fictional creepypasta. No reliable account of harm caused by viewing the image has ever been documented.
proponents: Michael Lutz (acknowledged author of the canonical text)
evidence_cited: Public revision history on Creepypasta Wiki
Coverage as fiction by Know Your Meme and Wikipedia

folklore.beliefs: Universally treated as fiction; the in-fiction 'curse' is part of the genre's chain-letter logic.

other: Subject of YouTube readings and animations

research.ongoing_studies: Studied within digital-folklore scholarship as a paradigm example of cursed-image creepypasta.
